query: Why do goal achievement rates differ across departments?

per_column.name: department_avg_completion
per_column.rationale: This is a department-level aggregate of the outcome itself (average completion per department). It restates the outcome at group level rather than supplying a candidate cause. It is neither a treatment nor a common cause of a treatment; it is a summary of the outcome, so it cannot serve as a confounder.

per_column.name: exceeds_dept_avg
per_column.rationale: A binary flag derived from comparing a record's completion to its department average. This is a re-encoding/discretization of the outcome, not an independent cause. It offers no treatment or confounder for causal estimation.

per_column.name: exceeds_overall_avg
per_column.rationale: Also a binary derivative of the outcome (completion vs overall average). Another outcome re-expression, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: status_numeric
per_column.rationale: A numeric encoding of state/status. State is largely a downstream reflection of achievement (post-treatment) or a re-encoding of progress, so it functions more as a mediator/outcome proxy than a genuine exogenous cause. It is not established as a common cause of any treatment and the outcome.

judge.rationale: The query asks WHY goal achievement differs across departments, requiring a candidate cause (treatment) whose effect on achievement is estimated, plus surfaced confounders that jointly cause treatment and outcome. None of the added columns supply a treatment: they are all derivatives of the outcome (department_avg_completion, exceeds_dept_avg, exceeds_overall_avg) or a status re-encoding (status_numeric) that is at best a mediator/outcome proxy. No variable plausibly causes both a treatment and the outcome, and nothing was surfaced from the data as a confounder. The operator constructed comparative outcome metrics rather than a causal estimation setup, so the technical claim for causal attribution is not satisfied.
